lines.text: Do you know how a sticky note sticks? Its glue was supposed to be a failure.
In 1968, a 3M scientist called Spencer Silver was trying to make a super strong glue. He made the opposite.
His glue was made of tiny sticky spheres. They only touch a surface at little points, so they hold lightly, and let go cleanly.
For years, nobody knew what to do with it. Then his colleague Art Fry wanted a bookmark that wouldn't fall out of his church hymn book.
A strip of that glue along one edge of a little paper square. They went on sale in 1980, and now they're everywhere.
Because the spheres don't flatten out, the same note can stick and peel again and again.
Orbi has quick notes too. Post a bubble, everyone gets their own colour, and it's gone within 30 minutes.
